name: Gregor Lang
role: Manager of the Neimmela Ranch, Medora; cattleman on the Little Missouri
bio: Gregor Lang was listed among the cattlemen of the Medora district at the stockmen's meeting of March 1884, and that month the paper marveled that his herd had gone two months without water and was still fat. He had a horse stolen from the Cantonment in April 1884, which was tracked and recovered, and in June 1884 he brought in another large lot of cattle carrying his new "triangle JP" brand. From July 1884 into early 1885 he ran a $50 reward notice for three missing mares and a pony, and in the March 1885 brand directory he appeared as manager of the Neimmela Ranch, Medora. In September 1885 he satisfied the Little Missouri River Stockgrowers' Association that a disputed branding had been lawful, and in December 1885 he settled George Fitzgerald's brand case by buying Fitzgerald's brand. He was on the Billings County ticket for justice in spring 1886, one of his hands, Henry Williams, won a steer-roping prize at the June 1886 round-up, and that September he sold his cattle at St. Paul.
